permalink.delete_yes: New interface, permanent link: button that confirms the deletion.
permalink.deleting: New interface, permanent link: progress message.
permalink.dns_taken: New interface, permanent link wizard: question after a name conflict; {host} is the address the owner typed.
permalink.done: New interface, permanent link wizard: shown when it succeeded; {host} is the address without the scheme.
permalink.help_domain: New interface, permanent link wizard: link to a help page, after a message that the domain is missing in Cloudflare.
permalink.help_login: New interface, permanent link wizard: link to a help page, after a failed login.
permalink.host_label: New interface, permanent link wizard, step 2: label of the address field.
permalink.host_placeholder: New interface, permanent link wizard, step 2: example address in the empty field.
permalink.intro: New interface, permanent link wizard: what the permanent link is and what it needs.
permalink.login_cancelled: New interface, permanent link wizard: shown after the owner cancelled the Cloudflare login.
permalink.login_failed: New interface, permanent link wizard: shown when the Cloudflare login failed without a reason.
permalink.login_link: New interface, permanent link wizard: link text, follows "If the page did not open:".
permalink.login_link_lead: New interface, permanent link wizard: followed by a link ("open the login page").
permalink.mode_named: New interface, Share view: the channel uses a permanent link; {host} is its address.
permalink.mode_quick: New interface, Share view: the channel uses a quick tunnel. trycloudflare.com is a domain name, keep it.
permalink.named_running: New interface, permanent link: message after switching back to it.
permalink.other_name: New interface, permanent link wizard: button after a name conflict.
permalink.overwrite: New interface, permanent link wizard: button after a name conflict; replaces the DNS record.
permalink.retry: New interface, permanent link wizard, step 1: button after a failed login.
permalink.setup: New interface, permanent link: button that opens the wizard.
permalink.starting: New interface, permanent link wizard: shown until the engine reports the login progress.
permalink.step_host: New interface, permanent link wizard, step 2.
permalink.step_login: New interface, permanent link wizard, step 1.
permalink.step_login_wait: New interface, permanent link wizard, step 1, while waiting for the login in the browser.
permalink.switching: New interface, permanent link: progress message.
permalink.waiting: New interface, permanent link wizard: shown while the login is not finished.
permalink.window_only: Note in a remote panel under the permanent link buttons.
permalink.wizard_label: New interface, permanent link wizard: accessible name of the wizard's panel.
player.about_time: New interface, player bar: screen-reader text of a position shown with "≈" (when copying the stream a seek lands on the previous keyframe).
player.added_by: New interface, player bar: second line under the title; {name} is the viewer's nick. Impersonal form (the program does not know the viewer's gender).
player.back_10: New interface, player bar: text of the small button that seeks 10 seconds back. Keep it as short as the English one.
player.back_10_label: New interface, player bar: tooltip and screen-reader name of the −10 s button.
player.copied: New interface: shown for a moment in place of "Copy link" after copying. Max ~16 characters.
player.copy_link: New interface, player bar: button text. Max ~16 characters.
player.copy_link_label: New interface, player bar: tooltip of the "Copy link" button.
player.copy_video_link: New interface, player menu (right click on the player bar): copies the source address of the video on air.
player.countdown: New interface, player bar: line under the title of the next video while the stream counts down to its start time; {time} is like 2:30.
player.forward_10: New interface, player bar: text of the small button that seeks 10 seconds forward. Keep it short.
player.forward_10_label: New interface, player bar: tooltip and screen-reader name of the +10 s button.
player.label: New interface, player bar at the bottom: accessible name of the bar (screen readers).
player.live: New interface, player bar: shown instead of the times for a live stream (it cannot be paused or seeked). Short, upper case.
player.obs_live: New interface, player bar: title while the OBS stream is on air (after an "OBS" tag). Max ~16 characters.
player.obs_live_hint: New interface, player bar: line under "OBS live".
player.obs_brb: New interface, player bar: title while the "be right back" slate airs after OBS dropped. Max ~16 characters.
player.obs_brb_hint: New interface, player bar: line under "Be right back".
player.obs_waiting: New interface, player bar: line under the video on air while OBS is connected and waits for it to end (priority off).
player.paused_obs: New interface, player bar: pause reason, the OBS stream holds the queue. Short.
player.menu: New interface: screen-reader name of the menu opened by a right click on the player bar.
player.mute: New interface, player bar: tooltip of the speaker button while the On air screen has sound.
player.next: New interface, player bar (⏭ button tooltip) and the player menu: skips the current video.
player.nothing_playing: New interface, player bar: title when no video is on air.
player.nothing_playing_hint: New interface, player bar: second line when no video is on air. One short line (it is cut with … when too long).
player.pause: New interface, player bar: tooltip of the big amber button while the channel plays (pauses the channel for all viewers).
player.pause_pending: New interface: second line of the player bar and label over the frozen left screen "Preview" after the owner paused at a moment the viewers have not got yet; the right screen (On air) keeps playing up to the end of the current segment (at most 4 s), then the channel pauses there. Max ~60 characters.
player.paused_manual: New interface, player bar: second line while the owner paused the channel.
player.paused_no_viewers: New interface, player bar: second line while the channel waits for a viewer (it resumes by itself).
player.paused_tunnel: New interface, player bar: second line while the channel waits for the internet connection (it resumes by itself).
player.position_of: New interface, player bar: screen-reader value of the timeline, e.g. "1:32 of 3:33".
player.restart: New interface, player bar (⏮ button tooltip) and the player menu: plays the current video again from 0:00 for everybody.
player.resume: New interface, player bar: tooltip of the big amber button while the owner paused the channel.
player.shortcuts: New interface, player menu: opens the list of keyboard shortcuts (also the ? key).
player.timeline: New interface, player bar: screen-reader name of the timeline (click or drag to seek).
player.unmute: New interface, player bar: tooltip of the speaker button while the On air screen is muted.
player.untitled: New interface: shown for a video whose source gave no title.
player.volume: New interface, player bar: screen-reader name of the volume slider. It changes only the On air screen in this window (the stream as the viewers get it), not the channel.
preview.copy_channel_link: New interface, context menu of the On air screen: copies the channel address for the VRChat video player.
preview.fallback: New interface, Channel view: small label in the corner of the Preview screen when it cannot play the video itself and shows the channel's own segments instead (it then reacts a few seconds after each control). Max ~36 characters.
preview.fallback_hint: New interface, Channel view: tooltip of the preview.fallback label.
preview.label: New interface: screen-reader name of the On air screen of the Channel view (the channel's stream as the viewers get it).
preview.menu: New interface: screen-reader name of the menu opened by a right click on the On air screen.
preview.preparing: New interface, Channel view: shown in the Preview screen while the program downloads a video from the internet so the Preview can play it itself (the first time only; then every control acts at once). Max ~40 characters.
preview.retry: New interface: button under the "On air unavailable" message (and "Preview unavailable" of the left screen); tries to play the stream again. Max ~20 characters.
preview.seek_bubble: New interface: bubble over the On air screen after the owner seeks. {seconds} is the measured delay of the On air screen, rounded.
preview.seek_bubble_unknown: New interface: bubble over the On air screen after a seek when the delay is not measured yet.
preview.sync: New interface, Channel view: button under the Preview while it plays the video itself (key S): the Preview jumps to where the channel is now; nothing changes for the viewers. Max ~34 characters.
preview.sync_hint: New interface, Channel view: tooltip of the preview.sync button.
preview.unavailable: New interface: message over the On air screen when the stream could not be played after several tries.
queue.add_button: New interface, Channel view: button next to the link field (the same as pressing Enter).
queue.add_label: New interface, Channel view: screen-reader label of the field where the owner pastes a link.
queue.add_placeholder: New interface, Channel view: placeholder of the link field. Keep the three dots.
queue.added_count: New interface: short message after several videos were added at once (a playlist or dropped files).
queue.added_one: New interface: short message after one link was added; {title} is the video title.
queue.adding: New interface, Channel view: shown on the button while the program reads the link. Keep the three dots.
queue.already_blocked: New interface, dialog "Remove the videos of this viewer?": shown instead of the block checkbox when the device is blocked already.
queue.also_block: New interface, dialog "Remove the videos of this viewer?": checkbox that also blocks the device of the viewer (the same block as Settings → Viewer nicks).
queue.anonymous: New interface, queue row: detail of a video a viewer added without a nick. Lower case, short.
queue.approve: New interface: tooltip of the check button that lets a viewer's video into the queue.
queue.approve_label: New interface: screen-reader label of the approve button; {title} is the video title.
queue.approve_list: New interface: tooltip of the check button that lets every video of a viewer's list into the queue.
queue.approve_list_label: New interface: screen-reader label of the button that approves every video of a viewer's list.
queue.by_host: New interface, queue row: detail of a video the owner added in the program (not a viewer). Lower case, short.
queue.clear: New interface, Channel view: small button in the queue heading that removes every waiting video (asks first); also the confirm button of that dialog. Max ~20 characters.
queue.clear_body: New interface, dialog "Clear the queue?": what will be removed. Waiting videos are those in the queue and those waiting for approval; the video on air is not among them.
queue.clear_title: New interface: title of the dialog that asks before the whole queue is cleared.
queue.copy_link: New interface, menu of a queued video: copies the address of the video.
queue.count: New interface, Channel view: number of videos in the queue, next to the heading (followed by their total length, e.g. "4 videos · 1:52:40").
queue.drop_hint: New interface, Channel view: small tip under the queue list, shown only in the program's own window (dropping files works only there, not in the remote panel).
queue.empty: New interface, Channel view: shown in the queue panel when nothing is waiting.
queue.obs_waits: New interface, queue panel: note at the top while the OBS stream is on air.
queue.from_disk: New interface, queue row: detail of a video that is a file on this computer. Lower case, short.
queue.include_on_air: New interface, dialogs "Clear the queue?" and "Remove the videos of this viewer?": checkbox (off by default) that also stops and removes the video on air; {title} is its title.
queue.list_heading: New interface, Channel view, Waiting for approval: heading of a group of videos one viewer sent as a list; {count} is the number of videos still waiting. Max ~30 characters.
queue.menu: New interface: accessible name of the context menu of a video in the queue.
queue.more: Screen-reader label of the ⋮ button on a queue row (phone layout); {title} is the video title.
queue.more_short: Tooltip of the ⋮ button on a queue row (phone layout).
queue.move_down: Queue context menu item: moves the video one place down.
queue.move_up: Queue context menu item: moves the video one place up.
queue.moved: New interface: announced to screen readers after a video was moved in the queue with the keyboard.
queue.next_failed: New interface, queue row: mark on the next video when preparing it ahead failed (it is tried again when it starts). Max ~14 characters.
queue.next_preparing: New interface, queue row: mark on the next video while the program prepares it ahead of its turn. Max ~18 characters.
queue.next_ready: New interface, queue row: mark on the next video when it is prepared and will start without a gap. Max ~12 characters.
queue.paste_not_link: New interface: error after Ctrl+V when the pasted text is not a web link.
queue.play_now: New interface, menu of a queued video: puts it on air at once.
queue.reject: New interface: tooltip of the cross button that refuses a viewer's video.
queue.reject_label: New interface: screen-reader label of the reject button; {title} is the video title.
queue.reject_list: New interface: tooltip of the cross button that refuses every video of a viewer's list.
queue.reject_list_label: New interface: screen-reader label of the button that rejects every video of a viewer's list.
queue.remove: New interface, menu of a queued video: removes it. Destructive action.
queue.remove_confirm: New interface, dialog "Remove the videos of this viewer?": the confirm button. Destructive action. Max ~20 characters.
queue.remove_requester: Queue context menu item (videos a viewer added): removes every waiting video of that viewer (same device, or same nick without a device); asks first. Max ~34 characters.
queue.remove_requester_body: New interface, dialog "Remove the videos of this viewer?": how many waiting videos (in the queue and waiting for approval) of the viewer will be removed.
queue.remove_requester_title: New interface: title of the dialog that asks before every waiting video of one viewer is removed.
queue.removed_blocked: New interface: added after the "videos removed" message when the device was blocked too.
queue.removed_count: New interface, Channel view: message under the queue after a bulk removal, next to the "Undo" button.
queue.reorder_hint: New interface: screen-reader hint of a queue row. Alt is the keyboard key.
queue.requested_anonymously: New interface, queue row waiting for approval: a viewer without a nick sent it.
queue.requested_by: New interface, queue row waiting for approval: who sent it; {name} is the viewer's nick. Impersonal form in Polish.
queue.restored_count: New interface: message after "Undo" put removed videos back.
queue.schedule: New interface, menu of a queued video: opens a dialog to set when the video starts (the stream counts down to it). Max ~24 characters.
queue.section_pending: New interface, Channel view: small heading over the videos that viewers sent and the owner has to approve (moderation switched on).
queue.section_queued: New interface, Channel view: small heading over the videos waiting to be played.

stats.row_connections: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, number of connections to Cloudflare and their locations.
stats.row_delay: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, how far behind the server the On air screen is, the buffered time and dropped video frames.
stats.row_encoder: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, the video encoder in use (for example h264_nvenc).

stats.row_format: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, technical parameters of the video file (resolution, frame rate, codecs).
stats.row_mode: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, whether the video is copied or converted.
stats.row_next_state: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, how far the preparation of the next video is.
stats.row_pause: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, whether the channel is paused and why.
stats.row_position: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, where the server is cutting the video (viewers are a few seconds behind).
stats.row_process: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, the ffmpeg process (PID, speed, CPU, memory).
stats.row_sequence: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, numbers of the HLS playlist.

stats.row_video: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, the title of the video and the site it comes from.
stats.row_watching: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): row label, number of different viewer addresses that fetched video in the last 30 seconds.
stats.title: New interface: title of the overlay with technical details over the On air screen (as on YouTube) and its screen-reader name; also the item of its right-click menu (key I).
stats.tunnel_connecting: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, the tunnel is starting.
stats.tunnel_error: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, the tunnel failed.
stats.tunnel_online: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, the tunnel works.
stats.tunnel_reconnecting: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, the tunnel lost its connection and tries again.
stats.v_about: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, "about N" (an approximate count).
stats.v_attempt: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, which attempt at playing the video this is (after a failure the program tries again).
stats.v_audio: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, the video has a sound track.
stats.v_behind: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, how far behind the server the On air screen is.

stats.v_connections: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, number of connections of the tunnel to Cloudflare.
stats.v_continuous: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, timestamps never went back (good).
stats.v_cpu: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, processor use of the process.
stats.v_discontinuities: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, number of discontinuity markers published (one for every change of video source).
stats.v_dropped: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, video frames the On air screen skipped.
stats.v_fps: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, frames per second. Keep it short.
stats.v_hours_minutes: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, a duration of hours and minutes.
stats.v_kb_s: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, data sent to viewers per second, in kilobytes.
stats.v_mb_s: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, data sent to viewers per second, in megabytes.
stats.v_minutes: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, a duration of minutes.
stats.v_mode_copy: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, the video is passed through as it is.
stats.v_mode_transcode: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, the video is converted to another format.
stats.v_next_failed: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, preparing the next video failed.
stats.v_next_preparing: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, the next video is being looked up and analysed.
stats.v_next_ready: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, the next video is being cut.
stats.v_no: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, plain "no".
stats.v_no_audio: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, the video has no sound track.
stats.v_not_continuous: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, timestamps went back at least once (bad).
stats.v_online_for: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, how long the tunnel has worked; {time} is a duration like "1 h 12 min".
stats.v_per_min: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, count per minute.

stats.v_reconnects: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, how many times the tunnel had to be started again.
stats.v_seconds: New interface, overlay "Stats for nerds" over the On air screen (like on YouTube): value, a duration of seconds.

ticker.added_by: Info ticker burned into the stream picture (seen by every viewer in VRChat), in the slate language. Who requested the video; {nick} is the viewer's nick. Impersonal form (the program does not know the gender).
ticker.added_by_host: Info ticker burned into the stream picture (seen by every viewer in VRChat), in the slate language. The video was added by the channel owner ("Host" is the owner's badge, also used next to queue items).
ticker.address: Info ticker burned into the stream picture (seen by every viewer in VRChat), in the slate language. {address} is the request page web address.
ticker.next: Info ticker burned into the stream picture (seen by every viewer in VRChat), in the slate language. The video after the current one; {title} is its title.
ticker.now: Info ticker burned into the stream picture (seen by every viewer in VRChat), in the slate language. Start of the ticker; {title} is the video on air. Keep the ► sign (the ticker font Arial has it; ▶ is not in Arial). Japanese uses ▶ instead: its ticker font Yu Gothic has no ►.
ticker.qr_caption: Info ticker burned into the stream picture (seen by every viewer in VRChat), in the slate language. Caption under the QR code in the corner of the stream picture (the code opens the request page). Very short.
titlebar.close: New interface, title bar: tooltip of the close button. Closing only hides the program to the notification area.
titlebar.failed: New interface, title bar: error message shown when a window button (minimize, maximize, close) or dragging the title bar did not work. {error} is the technical reason (usually English, from the window system).
titlebar.maximize: New interface, title bar: tooltip of the maximize button (same words as Windows uses).
titlebar.minimize: New interface, title bar of the window: tooltip of the minimize button (same words as Windows uses).
titlebar.restore: New interface, title bar: tooltip of the button that un-maximizes the window (same words as Windows uses).

tray.hidden_text: Tray icon of the desktop app. Text of the balloon shown once when the window is closed to the tray.
tray.hidden_title: Tray icon of the desktop app. Title of the balloon shown once when the window is closed to the tray. Keep the product name.
tray.link_without_internet: Tray icon of the desktop app. Added to a copied link when the tunnel is on but has no address yet: the link works only on this computer.
tray.net_connecting: Tray icon of the desktop app. Tooltip: the tunnel is starting. Used as {net} in tray.tooltip_head.
tray.net_manual: Tray icon of the desktop app. Tooltip: the tunnel is off and the owner typed an address. Used as {net} in tray.tooltip_head.
tray.net_offline: Tray icon of the desktop app. Tooltip: the tunnel is down. Used as {net} in tray.tooltip_head.
tray.net_online: Tray icon of the desktop app. Tooltip: the channel can be reached from the internet. Used as {net} in tray.tooltip_head.
tray.open_panel: Tray icon of the desktop app. Menu entry; opens the admin window. Max about 30 characters.
tray.quit: Tray icon of the desktop app. Menu entry; quits the program and stops the channel.
tray.skip: Tray icon of the desktop app. Menu entry; ends the video that is on air. Max about 30 characters.
tray.tooltip_head: Tray icon of the desktop app. Start of the tooltip; {net} is one of tray.net_*. Keep the product name VRCinema.
tray.tooltip_idle: Tray icon of the desktop app. Tooltip when no video is on air; {head} is the start of the tooltip. Windows keeps only about 127 characters of a tooltip.
tray.tooltip_playing: Tray icon of the desktop app. Tooltip while a video is on air; {title} is the video title (cut when too long).

viewer.copied: Request page: the copy button for a second after the channel address was copied.
viewer.copy: Request page: button that copies the channel address.
viewer.hint_any: Request page: hint under the form when any site is accepted.
viewer.howto_no_seek: Request page, 'How to watch in VRChat': third point. The channel is a live stream, so the in-world player cannot seek.
viewer.howto_paste: Request page, 'How to watch in VRChat': introduces the channel address in the box below.
viewer.howto_same_moment: Request page, 'How to watch in VRChat': second point.
viewer.howto_title: Request page: title of the collapsible section with instructions for VRChat.
viewer.howto_untrusted: Request page, 'How to watch in VRChat': first point. 'Allow Untrusted URLs', 'Settings' and 'Comfort & Safety' are the names in the VRChat menu; keep them in English (or as the game shows them in your language). 'Public', 'Group Public', 'Friends' and 'Invite' are VRChat's instance types; keep them as the game shows them. The second part is deliberately hedged ('may block'): since VRChat build 1546 the option no longer opens every address in Public and Group Public instances (the world's list of allowed domains decides there), which the project has not verified itself; it ends with what to try (a Friends or Invite instance). Informal address like the rest of the request page.
viewer.language: Request page: screen-reader name of the language selector (the selector lists the language names in themselves).
viewer.limit: Request page, under the form. {limit} is a length such as '2 h' or '30 min' (viewer.limit_hours / viewer.limit_minutes).
viewer.limit_hours: Request page: a length in hours inside viewer.limit; {n} is a number that may have one decimal.
viewer.limit_minutes: Request page: a length in minutes inside viewer.limit; {n} is a whole number.
viewer.link_label: Request page: label of the field for the video's address.
viewer.link_placeholder: Request page: example text shown in the empty link field.
viewer.live_stream: Request page, 'Now playing' card: shown beside the LIVE tag for a live stream (no progress bar).
viewer.moderation: Request page, under the form, after viewer.limit: new requests wait for the owner's approval.
viewer.nick_hint: Request page: small hint under the nick field. The nick appears next to the videos added with it. Impersonal wording.
viewer.nick_label: Request page: label of the optional nick field (maximum 24 characters).
viewer.now_playing: Request page: small heading of the card with the video that is playing now.
viewer.offline: Request page: shown at the top while the channel does not answer; the page retries by itself.
viewer.pin_adopt: Request page: button that binds this device to the viewer's nick after the PIN or recovery code. Informal. Max ~28 characters.
viewer.pin_adopted: Request page: message after the viewer's nick was adopted on this device; {nick} is the nick. Informal.
viewer.pin_checking: Request page: button text while the PIN is checked or saved. Max ~22 characters.
viewer.pin_code_done: Request page: button that closes the card with the recovery code once the viewer saved it. Max ~20 characters.
viewer.pin_code_text: Request page: text of the card with the one-time recovery code. Informal.
viewer.pin_code_title: Request page: heading of the card with the one-time recovery code. Informal.
viewer.pin_copied: Request page: short confirmation after copying the recovery code. Max ~20 characters.
viewer.pin_copy: Request page: button that copies the recovery code. Max ~20 characters.
viewer.pin_current_label: Request page: label of the field for the nick's current PIN (when changing it).
viewer.pin_hint: Request page: small hint under the PIN field: what a PIN may be.
viewer.pin_intro: Request page: text at the top of the PIN section. The channel's address changes when the owner restarts a quick tunnel; the PIN keeps the nick across that and across devices. Informal.
viewer.pin_its_mine: Request page: button after a nick was refused as taken; it opens the form for adopting the nick with its PIN. Informal.
viewer.pin_label: Request page: label of the PIN field (4–8 digits or a passphrase).
viewer.pin_new_label: Request page: label of the new PIN field when the recovery code is used.
viewer.pin_recovery_label: Request page: label of the recovery code field (XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX).
viewer.pin_save: Request page: button that saves the PIN of the viewer's nick. Max ~22 characters.
viewer.pin_saved: Request page: message after the PIN was saved; {nick} is the nick. Informal.
viewer.pin_sign_out: Request page: checkbox when adopting a nick: the viewer's other devices lose the nick (they need the PIN again). Informal.
viewer.pin_tab_adopt: Request page: tab of the PIN section for using the nick on this device with the PIN. Informal. Max ~24 characters.
viewer.pin_tab_set: Request page: tab of the PIN section for setting the PIN. Max ~24 characters.
viewer.pin_toggle: Request page: summary line that opens the PIN section under the nick field. Informal.
viewer.pin_use_pin: Request page: link-like button that switches from the recovery code back to the PIN.
viewer.pin_use_recovery: Request page: link-like button that switches from the PIN to the recovery code (when the PIN is forgotten). Informal.
viewer.send_failed: Request page: shown under the form when a request could not be sent at all (no connection, or no answer in time). The page does not send it again by itself, so the viewer is asked to check the connection and press the button again. Informal like the rest of the request page.
viewer.paused: Request page: small tag in the 'Now playing' heading when the owner paused the channel.
viewer.pending: Request page: short message after a request that waits for the owner's approval. {title} is the video's title.
viewer.progress: Request page: screen-reader name of the progress bar of the playing video.
viewer.queue_empty: Request page: shown instead of the 'Up next' list when it is empty.
viewer.sites_none: Request page: the owner allows only listed sites, but the list is empty, so every link is refused.
viewer.sites_title: Request page: introduces the list of sites that work (shown only when the owner allows listed sites only). Ends with a colon; the sites follow.
viewer.title: Request page: heading and browser tab title (the channel has no name of its own).
viewer.use_nick: Request page: button after a nick was refused as taken; it fills the field with a free alternative. {nick} is that nick.
viewer.your_icon: Request page: screen-reader name and tooltip of the viewer's own small icon beside the nick field.
units.seconds: A duration in seconds, inside other messages.
wizard.done: Wizard, internet step: button that ends the wizard once the channel is on the internet.
wizard.encoder_cpu: Wizard step 3: result when only the processor can be used.
wizard.encoder_failed: Wizard step 3: the test failed; {error} is the reason.
wizard.encoder_gpu: Wizard step 3: result, under the name of the card type.
wizard.encoder_intro: Wizard step 3: why the test is made.
wizard.encoder_skip: Wizard step 3: button after a failed test that goes on.
wizard.encoder_testing: Wizard step 3: shown while the test runs.
wizard.language_hint: First wizard step: hint under the language choice.
wizard.language_title: First wizard step: heading of the language choice (a list of buttons with the language names).
wizard.net_changes: Wizard step 4: note under the links about the quick link and the permanent link.
wizard.net_channel_link: Wizard step 4: label of the channel link (the .m3u8 address). VRChat is a game name, keep it.
wizard.net_connecting: Wizard step 4: shown while the connection is being made.
wizard.net_failed: Wizard step 4: the connection failed (no reason given).
wizard.net_intro: Wizard step 4: what happens. VRChat is a game name, keep it.
wizard.net_qr_alt: Wizard step 4: alternative text of the QR code image.
wizard.net_qr_hint: Wizard step 4: next to the QR code.
wizard.net_request_link: Wizard step 4: label of the address of the page where viewers add videos.
wizard.net_retrying: Wizard step 4: shown while the connection is lost and the program retries.
wizard.net_skip_hint: Wizard step 4: what can be done when there is no connection.
wizard.next: Wizard: button that goes to the next step.
wizard.permanent: Wizard, internet step: button that ends the wizard and opens Settings, Internet, where the permanent link is set up.
wizard.progress: Wizard: accessible label of the row of progress dots.
wizard.retry: Wizard: button that repeats a failed step.
wizard.skip: Wizard, internet step: button that ends the wizard without the internet connection.
wizard.start: Button of the first wizard step that goes to the downloading of the tools.
wizard.step: Wizard: which step is shown; {n} is the step, {total} the number of steps.
wizard.tools_failed: Wizard step 2: the download failed; {error} is the reason.
wizard.tools_incomplete: Wizard step 2: the download ended but a tool is still missing (used as the {error} of the failure message).
wizard.tools_present: Wizard step 2: nothing had to be downloaded.
wizard.tools_ready: Wizard step 2: the download is finished.
wizard.tools_skip: Wizard step 2: button after a failed download that ends the wizard and opens the program.
wizard.welcome_intro: First wizard step: what the program does. VRChat is a game name, keep it.
wizard.welcome_setup: First wizard step: what the setup will do.
wizard.welcome_title: Title of the first wizard step (first run of the program).
volume.preview: New interface, player bar: screen-reader name and tooltip of the first of two volume sliders; it changes only what the host hears from the Preview screen, not the channel.
volume.preview_tag: New interface, player bar: tiny label before the Preview's volume slider (two sliders side by side). Max ~8 characters.
volume.air_tag: New interface, player bar: tiny label before the On air volume slider (two sliders side by side). Max ~8 characters.
screens.swap: New interface, Channel view: small button (tooltip, screen-reader label) on the small screen in the corner: the small and the big screen change places (a click on the small screen does the same).
screens.pip: New interface, Channel view: small button on the On air screen while it stands beside the Preview: On air becomes a small screen in the Preview's corner.
screens.side: New interface, Channel view: small button on the small screen: the Preview and On air stand side by side, the same size.
screens.tools: New interface, Channel view: screen-reader name of the group of small layout buttons on a screen (not shown).
screens.window: New interface, Channel view: small button: the On air screen moves to a window of its own (e.g. for a second monitor; it can stay always on top).
screens.away: New interface, Channel view: note in the Preview's corner while the On air screen has a window of its own; a "Bring back" button follows. Max ~44 characters.
screens.bring_back: New interface, Channel view: button after screens.away: On air comes back into the main window (its own window closes). Max ~16 characters.
screens.on_top: New interface, the On air screen's own window: switch that keeps the window above all other windows (remembered). Max ~26 characters.
settings.channel.viewer_list_max: New interface, Settings view, Channel: label of the number field (most videos one viewer list adds).
settings.channel.viewer_list_max_hint: New interface, Settings view, Channel: hint of the number field; the same number caps the entries read from a playlist.
settings.channel.viewer_list_max_invalid: New interface, Settings view, Channel: error when the list size is not a whole number from 1 to 50.
settings.channel.viewer_list_max_saved: New interface, Settings view, Channel: confirmation after the list size was saved.
settings.channel.viewer_lists: New interface, Settings view, Channel: switch that lets viewers send several links at once and playlists.
settings.channel.viewer_lists_block: New interface, Settings view, Channel: heading of the block about viewer lists. Max ~30 characters.
settings.channel.viewer_lists_hint: New interface, Settings view, Channel: hint of the viewer lists switch.
settings.channel.viewer_lists_off: New interface, Settings view, Channel: confirmation after the viewer lists switch was turned off.
settings.channel.viewer_lists_on: New interface, Settings view, Channel: confirmation after the viewer lists switch was turned on.
viewer.checking_links: Request page: shown on the button while the links of a list are being checked; {count} is the number of links sent.
viewer.links_hint: Request page: hint under the multi-line link field; {count} is how many videos one list may add.
viewer.links_label: Request page, shown when the owner allows lists: label of the multi-line field for several video links.
viewer.links_placeholder: Request page: placeholder of the multi-line link field. Max ~40 characters.
viewer.list_added: Request page: result after sending a list; {count} videos went into the queue.
viewer.list_line: Request page: names a left-out link of a list that has no title, by its line number {line} in the field.
viewer.list_pending: Request page: result after sending a list while the owner approves requests; {count} videos wait for approval.
viewer.list_skipped: Request page: result after sending a list; {count} links or playlist entries were left out (the reasons are listed below it).
trim.bad_time: New interface, notice after the trim dialog: a time field held something that is not a time.
trim.clear: New interface, trim dialog: button that removes both points (the whole video plays).
trim.hint: New interface, trim dialog: note under the time fields.
trim.in: New interface, trim dialog: label of the start time field. Max ~16 characters.
trim.out: New interface, trim dialog: label of the end time field. Max ~16 characters.
trim.title: New interface: title of the trim dialog (where a queued video starts and ends on air).
trim.use_preview: New interface, trim dialog: button next to a time field; fills in where the Preview stands now (only for the video in the Preview).
schedule.at: New interface, start-time dialog: label of the clock time field (today, or tomorrow when the time has passed). Max ~16 characters.
schedule.bad_time: New interface, notice after the start-time dialog: no valid time was entered.
schedule.clear: New interface, start-time dialog: button that removes the start time (the video plays when its turn comes).
schedule.hint: New interface, start-time dialog: note under the fields.
schedule.in: New interface, start-time dialog: label before the buttons +1 min, +2 min, … Max ~20 characters.
schedule.minutes: New interface, start-time dialog: a button that starts the video in {minutes} minutes. Max ~16 characters.
schedule.title: New interface: title of the dialog that sets when a queued video starts.
meter.clip: New interface, Channel view: label and tooltip of the red light of the level meter; it lights for 3 s when the sound reaches full scale.
meter.label: New interface, Channel view: screen-reader name of the level meter beside the Preview and On air (peak bars, loudness in LUFS, clipping light).
meter.title: New interface, Channel view: tooltip of the level meter; dBFS and LUFS are units, keep them.
